inputs.text: Senate Bill 175 is being sold as a modest safeguard, but limiting new registrants’ access to state elections is still a decision to make participation harder. Appeals to “confidence” can disguise exclusion as good governance, shifting the burden onto voters rather than fixing institutions. The right to vote should be accessible; any rule that narrows participation deserves scrutiny, not automatic trust.
